title: A family of shapes
description:
Write a small class hierarchy:

```python
class Shape(ABC):            # abstract: area() and perimeter() are abstract methods
    def describe(self): ...  # "<Name>: area 12.00, perimeter 14.00", with the class name

class Rectangle(Shape):  def __init__(self, width, height)
class Square(Rectangle): def __init__(self, side)              # a square IS a rectangle
class Circle(Shape):     def __init__(self, radius)            # use math.pi

def largest(shapes): ...     # the shape with the greatest area (the first one on a tie); None for an empty list
def total_area(shapes): ...  # works for any objects that have an area() method, shapes or not
```

`Shape()` itself must raise `TypeError` (it is abstract). `describe` is written only once, in `Shape`; `type(self).__name__` gives the class name.
hints: Mark `area` and `perimeter` with `@abstractmethod` in `Shape(ABC)`; Python then refuses to create a `Shape` and checks that subclasses provide them.
